card.name: Puxada de Rede
card.tagline: Bahian fishermen's dramatic net-pulling dance honoring Iemanja.
card.profile: Puxada de rede ('pulling of the net') is a Brazilian folkloric theatrical dance from Bahia/the Northeast, often performed within capoeira shows. Based on a legend of a fisherman who drowns at sea and whose body is found in the net, it dramatizes the labor and grief of traditional xareu net-fishing and invokes Iemanja, goddess of the sea. Danced to a slow atabaque beat with songs and synchronized net-pulling movements; families sing and clap on the beach (English Wikipedia; Mandingueira).
card.insight: The tradition is rooted in the post-slavery period when freed people turned to artisanal fishing in Santo Amaro, Bahia; the artisanal practice has declined since the 1970s (English Wikipedia).
